text:
olga: Heads up — after the calico-ebpf 3.29 rollout to eu-west1 we started seeing intermittent RDMA handshake failures and a spike in east-west latency for GPU pods. Training queues are backing up. @oncall-sre please take.
kevin: seeing same — pods on node gpu-eu-12 -> gpu-eu-15 show high p95 latency ~120ms for gRPC, normally ~2-4ms. RDMA connect errors in training logs: "rdma_connect: ret=-110 (TIMEDOUT)".
maria: grabbed tcpdump between pod IPs, I can share snippet. Here's a short capture showing SYN then no ACK for reaps on packet size ~1500: 
```
15:02:12.345 IP pod-12 > pod-15: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, length 0
15:02:12.345 IP pod-15 > pod-12: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, length 0
15:02:12.456 IP pod-12 > pod-15: Flags [ACK], seq 1, ack 1, length 0
... then large gaps (100-200ms)
```
kevin: also ran `iperf3 -c` between the pods — saw large jitter and throughput collapse around MTU boundary. suspect fragmentation/encap mismatch. `ip link show` shows mtu 1450 on calico hostdev interface, but underlying tunnel MTU 9000 on host.
maria: checked cni config: `bpf-mtu: 1420`, `tproxy: enabled`, `encap: vxlan` on some nodes and `ipip` on others — looks like mixed encap after canary.
infra-bot: Deploy bot: calico-ebpf 3.29 rollout to eu-west1 completed 2026-03-18T15:00:05Z (50% nodes). Rollout ID: rb-2026-03-18-3.29
jonathan: RDMA stacks are very sensitive to asymmetric routing and MTU. If traffic is being tproxied or rerouted through host stack with different MTU, handshake (MAD/CM) can stall. Getting "ibv_reg: Fragmented WR" in some kworker logs.
oncall-sre: taking ownership. Immediate action: pause remaining rollout in eu-west1 and start rollback on canary nodes. @infra-bot can you pin calico-ebpf to 3.28 for the rest of the fleet?
infra-bot: Action queued: rollback plan to calico-ebpf 3.28 initiated for nodes tagged eu-west1-canary. ETA 8m.
olga: We're also seeing GPU job queue increase 3x, reserved capacity autoscale kicked in and we're burning extra cloud credits. Need to notify cost-ops and throttle noncritical training jobs.
kevin: steps I'm running now: 1) collect `ethtool -k` on affected NICs, 2) check host routes (`ip route show table main`), 3) dump iptables nat PREROUTING/TPROXY rules. Posting outputs in thread shortly.
maria: workaround for now is pinning RDMA-critical workloads to nodes still on 3.28 (label `cni-v=3.28`) — moving a few canary jobs helped restore handshakes.
jonathan: long term we should add RDMA smoke tests to CNI upgrade pipeline, and a MTU/encap compatibility check. Also, don't mix encap modes mid-rollout.
oncall-sre: creating incident INC-2026-0427 for tracking. Assigning to eng-infra, eng-runtime, and ml-infra. Will open postmortem if rollback doesn't fully resolve.
olga: thanks. I'll get cost-ops in the loop and schedule a quick cross-team sync with product teams impacted. :eyes: 
kevin: attaching quick commands I used:
```
kubectl get pods -n gpu-fleet -o wide | grep pod-12
kubectl logs -n gpu-fleet pod-12 -c trainer | grep rdma
ethtool -k ens10
iptables -t mangle -S | grep TPROXY
```
olga: keep updates here. If rollback clears things, we'll re-run a canary with explicit MTU/encap gates and RDMA smoke test.
